A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same MEMOED study. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–H support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original analyses of OLMo-7B generations for 110 cultures, human annotation comparisons in Section 4.2, and ablation results in Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains the original generation analyses, human annotation results and ablations, including the food and clothing classification scores in Section 4.2.

M1.justification: MEMOED retains the same document filtering, contribution scores, z-score classification and generalization procedures. Section 3.4 corrects confusing wording about weak-association mapping without establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both study food and clothing across 110 cultures, with the same annotation and model-variant subsets. The six topics removed from Table 9 were not evaluated in either version.

E2.justification: The human-label validation and OLMo-7B-0424 comparisons are retained. No evaluated comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Generation settings, 300 generations per culture per topic, annotation design and Appendix F ablation protocols remain unchanged. Table 9 retains identical filtering keywords for the two evaluated topics.

E4.justification: Appendix F retains the sampling-parameter, model-variant and z-score ablations. The topic-modeling case studies, document excerpts and Appendix H leave-one-culture-out analysis also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting remains unchanged, including the correlation and weighted-F1 summaries. Neither version adds seed information, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Reported scores, counts, rankings and plotted findings are unchanged, including weighted F1 of 0.845 for clothing and 0.670 for food. Appendix F.2 completes a sentence describing stronger positive correlations already numerically reported in v1.

T1.justification: The distance metrics, document signal-to-noise ratio, contribution score, classification criteria and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Rephrasing the association descriptions does not introduce new formal definitions, assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the MEMOED attribution contribution and findings about cultural-frequency imbalances. The suggested use with unlearning or data augmentation retains the same scientific scope.

C2.justification: The explanations of memorization, diffuse association and cross-culture generalization remain substantively unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning document-level attribution and applicability beyond the OLMo family.

D1.justification: Table 9 removes preprocessing keyword lists for six topics outside the reported study, while preserving the food and clothing lists. Other implementation details, prompts, hyperparameters and code/data access statements are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list retain the same cited works and research positioning. Citation punctuation corrections do not change the relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: v2 makes local grammar and terminology corrections, fixes a double negative in Section 3.4, completes an unfinished sentence in Appendix F.2 and corrects a section reference. It also adds acknowledgments and updates the publication header; the overall organization remains stable.

P2.justification: Table 9 contracts from eight topic rows to two, changing its layout and the subsequent appendix text flow. An acknowledgments page is inserted, while all 17 figures and the remaining table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity by repairing v1's confusing weak-association wording and unfinished correlation sentence, correcting a section reference, and aligning Table 9 with the studied topics. These are useful editorial corrections; the method, empirical evidence and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
